forces.title: Persistent high input costs and inflation pressure margins
forces.description: Food and beverage producers, including packaged food manufacturers, continue to face severe margin pressure from high energy, staffing, and transport costs. Global commodity prices for key inputs like cereals, oils, and sugar have risen, contributing to overall food inflation across Europe. Over 91% of food businesses reported increased operating costs in 2025, with 85% anticipating further increases in 2026, leading to ongoing profitability tightening.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical conflict and trade tensions disrupt supply chains
forces.description: The Middle East conflict and other geopolitical uncertainties are leading to freight and logistics surcharges, energy price hikes, and supply chain delays. Disruptions in critical trade routes, like the Strait of Hormuz, impact fertilizer and grain shipments, threatening food security and increasing input costs. This volatility demands increased working capital and creates an unpredictable operating environment for packaged food and snack producers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Evolving EU regulations increase compliance and operational burden
forces.description: New EU regulations significantly impact packaged food and snack manufacturers. The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) from August 2026 introduces recyclability, labelling, and substance restrictions. The Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) from December 2026 demands deforestation-free verification for commodities like palm oil, cocoa, and soy. Enhanced food safety rules on Listeria for ready-to-eat foods also add compliance requirements, driving up operational complexity and costs across the value chain.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Growing consumer demand for value, private-label, and premium offerings
forces.description: Consumer purchasing decisions for packaged foods are increasingly driven by a reevaluation of value, leading to shifts towards private-label substitutes and premium offerings with added benefits. Retailers are actively developing sophisticated multi-tiered private brand strategies, often with better quality perception and lower prices than national brands. This intensifies competition and requires incumbent brands to innovate with distinctive products to maintain relevance and market share against these alternatives.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Increased investment in automation, digitalisation, and AI enhances efficiency
forces.description: Food and beverage producers, including those in packaged foods, are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods to boost productivity, counteract labor shortages, and manage costs. Digitalization efforts focus on traceability, compliance, and data management for better decision-making. The adoption of AI is evolving from experimentation to practical implementation, supporting quality control, predictive maintenance, and supply chain management, offering a pathway to improved operational efficiency and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Extreme weather impacts harvests and raw material costs
forces.description: Western Europe experienced exceptionally high temperatures and very low rainfall in summer 2026, leading to significant weather volatility. These extreme conditions are affecting harvests and the availability and cost of raw materials for food and drink production across Europe. For the tillage sector, reduced planted areas and unfavorable ripening conditions due to hot weather point to a negative outlook for cereal tonnage, directly increasing input costs for packaged food processors.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Consumer shift towards healthier, functional, and transparent products
forces.description: Consumers are increasingly prioritizing healthiness, with 57% ranking it among their top three decision factors. This translates into active seeking of protein, fiber, and nutrient-dense foods, while avoiding artificial flavors, sweeteners, sugar, and highly processed items. Packaged food companies must offer simpler ingredients, clearer benefits, and fewer perceived trade-offs. This trend presents both an opportunity for innovation in healthy snacks and processed foods, and a challenge for traditional high-sugar/fat categories.
forces.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

forces.title: GLP-1 adoption threatens consumption of high-calorie snacks and drinks
forces.description: The growing adoption of Glucagon-like peptide-1s (GLP-1s) medications is projected to materially alter consumer food purchasing habits. Early data indicates that active GLP-1 users are significantly cutting back on categories such as chips, savory snacks, sweet snacks, and soft drinks. This trend poses a substantial risk to packaged food and snack manufacturers whose portfolios heavily rely on high-calorie, high-sugar, and high-fat items, necessitating a strategic pivot towards healthier, protein-rich alternatives to mitigate future volume declines.
forces.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

forces.title: Consumer spending shifts from at-home CPGs to away-from-home food
forces.description: Consumers are increasingly diverting their food spending from at-home CPGs, including packaged foods, towards food away from home (restaurants, takeout, delivery). In the US, this share is estimated to reach 58% by 2025, and food delivery platforms are expanding in Europe, blurring the lines between dining out and at-home consumption. This trend necessitates CPGs to innovate products that offer convenience, shorten meal preparation, or enhance the at-home experience, as well as leverage new distribution channels like delivery platforms.
forces.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

forces.title: Rise of nimble disruptor brands challenging incumbent growth
forces.description: Small, independent disruptor brands are increasingly accounting for a disproportionate share of growth in the F&B market, particularly in categories like specialty oils, seasonings, and functional shakes. These brands are perceived by consumers to deliver superior functional benefits, even at a price premium, competing effectively against both private labels (on function) and large incumbents. This forces established packaged food companies to move beyond incremental innovation and create truly distinctive, function-forward products.
forces.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

forces.title: Accelerated algorithmic price discovery and market volatility
forces.description: Agricultural commodity markets, which are critical for packaged food inputs, are experiencing faster price discovery driven by algorithms and quantamental signals from new market entrants, including hedge funds and sophisticated commodity buyers. This compresses the time traders and processors have to react to supply and demand shifts. Leading players are adopting AI, machine learning, and satellite imagery for real-time logistics and predictive insights, necessitating increased agility and analytical sophistication from all market participants.
forces.source_title: How agility and AI could rewire agriculture trading

forces.title: Increased working capital demand due to market volatility and interest rates
forces.description: Heightened uncertainty surrounding inflation and the physical availability of fertilizer and fuel, combined with ongoing changes in interest rates, has amplified pressure on working capital requirements for agricultural trading houses and processors, including those in packaged foods. Market players face elevated capital costs for carrying inventories and increased collateral for margin obligations at commodity exchanges. This financial strain demands robust cash management and flexible funding solutions to navigate market volatility effectively.
forces.source_title: How agility and AI could rewire agriculture trading

forces.title: Biofuel policies impact edible oil and grain markets
forces.description: Government policies promoting renewable diesel, particularly in the US and Indonesia, have significantly impacted oilseed markets. This has spurred investment in crushing capacity and initially elevated soybean oil futures prices and crush margins. However, as new facilities come online, soybean crush margins have decreased by up to 80%. These shifts create volatility for edible oil manufacturers and grain processors within the packaged foods sector, necessitating adaptive sourcing and pricing strategies in response to energy market linkages.
forces.source_title: How agility and AI could rewire agriculture trading

forces.title: UK sugar levy threshold lowered, restricting unhealthy foods
forces.description: The UK government has proposed lowering the Soft Drinks Industry Levy (SDIL) sugar threshold from 5g to 4.5g of added sugar per 100ml. This regulatory change directly impacts packaged food and snack manufacturers that use sugar as an ingredient, particularly in confectionery, baked goods, and other processed foods. It will necessitate product reformulation to avoid the levy, potentially increasing production costs or altering consumer preferences for affected products.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Prepared consumer foods exports demonstrate resilience amidst broader sector decline
viewpoints.description: In H1 2026, the Irish food and beverage sector experienced a 3% decline in overall exports. However, prepared consumer foods stood out as the only subsector to match its exceptionally strong performance from 2025. This indicates a relative resilience for packaged food products compared to other categories like meat, dairy, beverages, seafood, and horticulture, which all saw declines. Despite high input costs, this segment maintained its export value, highlighting its stable demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish food and beverage operators positive on opportunities despite challenging environment
viewpoints.description: A Q2 2026 customer survey by Love Irish Food and Bank of Ireland revealed that 62% of operators in the Irish food and beverage sector are positive about their business opportunities. This optimism persists despite a wider environment outlook that is less favorable than in previous years, characterized by ongoing cost pressures, inflation, and market uncertainties. The sentiment suggests an underlying confidence in the sector's ability to innovate and adapt.
viewpoints.source_firm: Love Irish Food and Bank of Ireland
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Agrifood sector shows selective resilience amidst cost pressures
viewpoints.description: Ireland’s agrifood sector, which includes packaged foods and snacks through its processing activities, demonstrated selective resilience in Q2 2026. While underlying momentum is evident, profitability is tightening due to rising fuel, processing, and transport costs linked to the Middle East conflict. The sector's performance in the near term is dependent on how these cost conditions, demand trends, and the broader macroeconomic environment evolve. Businesses are advised to monitor costs and liquidity closely.

viewpoints.title: Greek Food & Beverage industry resilient with strong growth prospects
viewpoints.description: The Greek Food and Beverage industry, encompassing packaged foods, is identified as a crucial and resilient pillar of the Greek economy. It contributes significantly to GDP and exports, demonstrating a dynamic and competitive presence in European and global markets. Despite challenges like rising energy costs, inflation, and foreign competition, the sector maintains strong growth prospects due to high product quality, export momentum, and a consumer shift towards healthier foods, indicating robust long-term potential.
viewpoints.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

viewpoints.title: Rising commodity prices for cereals, oils, and sugar drive food index upwards
viewpoints.description: Teagasc reports that international price developments for agri-commodities in 2026 show rising prices for cereals, oils, and sugar, while dairy and meat prices have been falling. The FAO Monthly Food Price Index is moving upwards in 2026, reaching its highest level since early 2023. This indicates a general increase in raw material costs for packaged food manufacturers, suggesting continued inflationary pressure on the sector's input side, despite some offsetting declines in other commodities.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Food & Beverage sector resilient despite multiple external pressures
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland observes that the Irish food and beverage sector has maintained its resilience in early 2026, even when faced with global conflicts, rising operational costs, stricter EU regulatory requirements, and evolving consumer demands. Although export values were flat year-on-year in January-February 2026, the sector has demonstrated adaptability. High input costs persist, particularly for ingredients like wheat, sugar, and cocoa, suggesting ongoing margin challenges for packaged food producers.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Incumbent F&B CPGs face sustained pressure without growth model shift
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that the long-standing growth model for F&B Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies, including those in packaged foods, has reached its limits. Without a significant shift in how they generate growth, incumbent CPGs are likely to face sustained pressure on both volume and profitability. This is driven by constrained volume gains, underperformance relative to the broader market, and increasing competition from private labels and disruptor brands, necessitating strategic portfolio reshaping and brand relevance.
viewpoints.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

viewpoints.title: Large CPG brands lack meaningful edge against private label and disruptors
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's analysis indicates that large packaged food and beverage CPG brands are increasingly 'caught in the middle' without a distinct competitive edge. Private labels consistently win on price, offering comparable or superior quality at lower costs. Simultaneously, smaller disruptor brands excel on functional benefits, attracting consumers willing to pay a premium. This dynamic means large incumbents struggle to differentiate, facing a significant challenge to justify their value proposition in an evolving, price- and function-sensitive market.
viewpoints.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth

demand_drivers.description: 61% of consumers globally state price matters more, and cost/value perception are top reasons for brand switching.

demand_drivers.driver: Demand for 'better' products with functional benefits
demand_drivers.description: Consumers are willing to pay more for products delivering differentiated function, quality, or experiences, especially high-protein, fiber, and nutrient-dense foods.
Consumers are increasingly cooking from scratch to manage food costs, impacting demand for ready-to-eat meals but boosting demand for basics, spices, oils, and sauces.

new_opportunities.description: Agricultural processors are investing in specialty oils, alternative-protein processing, and functional health markets to reduce earnings volatility and cater to evolving consumer preferences.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Diversification into specialty and downstream products

new_opportunities.description: Consumers seek high-protein, fiber, and nutrient-dense foods. Disruptor brands successfully combine indulgent flavors with functional benefits (e.g., high protein, low sugar) to compete in traditional snack categories.
CPG companies can offer products that reduce friction, shorten meal-preparation time, or elevate the at-home food experience, and leverage delivery platforms for new channels and product testing.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Developing products for at-home convenience and delivery platforms

market_sizing.methodology: The report highlights intensified competition for packaged foods and snacks from private labels and disruptor brands. Consumers prioritize value and benefits, leading to shifts in spending patterns. Retailers are enhancing private-label strategies by leveraging real-time data for product formulation and pricing, allowing them to rapidly introduce new offerings and capture market share. National brands must create distinctive products to compete effectively.
market_sizing.source_title: State of Food and Beverage: The choices CPG leaders can make to renew growth
